newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta reviews Europe cargo structures, agents.
newsitem.headline: Delta reviews Europe cargo structures, agents.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said it has appointed new cargo general sales agents for the Netherlands and Belgium as part of a Europe sales re-structuring.

Danita Waterfall, Delta's regional director cargo sales and services Europe, said she has named Aero Freight as gsa for Belgium with effect from August 1 and Zygene for the Netherlands from September 1.
The two gsas replace Delta staff in both countries, she told Reuters in an interview.

Waterfall, who took on the new Europe cargo director post in March, said she was reviewing the airline's entire structure in Europe where sales is largely in the hands of agents and handling is conducted by different companies.
"In this first year it is necessary for us to look at each city one by one and see if the gsa that has always been there is the best solution to our cargo needs," she said.
"Now that Delta wants to be a more serious player it may make more sense to have some of our own people," she added.
Criteria include the readiness of gsas to change in accordance with the new Delta products and structure, she noted.
This could mean appointing new agents or Delta staff, according to local market needs, although she was broadly satisfied with the current agents.
Another innovation was to ask sales agents to manage import handling, including documentation, customer contacts and shipment tracing.
"What we are doing is getting the gsas to handle export and import functions. We are really trying to streamline," Waterfall added.
"We are doing this in London quite successfully, and we have started in Milan and Rome where it is already working very well," she noted.
Delta is also looking at more trucking routes in co-operation with forwarders, including cross-border services.
Another change is that European agents now report to Frankfurt rather than Atlanta, she said.
In Frankfurt, sales have been centralised and a toll-free cargo reservations number has been launched.
"Delta in the past has tried to figure out what to do from Atlanta. A real goal is to look at Europe separately and from what Atlanta might think," she explained.

One example was her decision to locate the Europe office in Frankfurt, the airline's largest European market, instead of in London, as the head office had originally planned. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
